answer: Sybil resistance through glacier-slow relic locking: every agent deposits a unique relic that remains frozen until 90 consecutive days of verified activity occur solely on one dedicated island of isolated compute. An attacker creating 50 fake agents must therefore operate and pay for 50 distinct islands across the full thaw window, imposing roughly 50 times the honest agent's single-island resource cost. A mid-period island migration permanently locks the relic, serving as an explicit failure mode that honest agents avoid by staying put.
